mainTopic: Doubtful firstborn animals: the priestly gifts, dividing a surviving animal, and cases of two ewes giving birth
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of רבי יוסי, who exempts a ספק בכור from the priestly gifts because its replacement is already with the כהן. The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר still needed to say that this is רבי יוסי's real reason. Next, רב פפא rules that everyone, even רבי מאיר, exempts a ספק מעשר from the gifts. The גמרא challenges this twice and shows why his statement was still needed. The גמרא then turns to the case where one of two possible firstborns died. רבי טרפון says the כהן and the owner divide the survivor, and רבי אמי explains that רבי טרפון retracted his earlier view. רבי חייא gives two parables, a shepherd and a homeowner, and רבא explains that everyone accepts both rules. They argue only when the animals are in the owner's courtyard and the shepherd is a כהן: does the owner give the כהן a share for the sake of the מצוה? A new משנה then lays out cases of two ewes giving birth together. The גמרא begins explaining why each case had to be taught, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי's words to show רבי אלעזר's point is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי יוסי's ruling and infers from its wording that the exemption depends on the replacement being with the כהן. That would make רבי אלעזר's statement unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of the כהן is exempt from the gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates it. So if the replacement is with the כהן, yes, it is exempt. If the replacement is not with the כהן, no, it is not exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רבי אלעזר. It quotes רבי יוסי's own words, which already seem to say what רבי אלעזר said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר explained that רבי יוסי's reason is that the 'replacement' is with the כהן. But רבי יוסי's own wording, 'כל שחליפיו ביד כהן', already makes the exemption depend on that. So why did רבי אלעזר need to say it at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Replacement; here, the other animal that already went to the כהן in place of this one
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal
Obligates; holds that one must give
Yes / No: the גמרא's way of drawing an inference from the wording

phrases.english: Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of the priest
is exempt from the gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates it.
Replacement in the priest's hand: yes, it is exempt,
no replacement in the priest's hand: no, it is not exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the 'פשיטא' challenge against רבי אלעזר that began just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that רבי יוסי's reason is that the replacement is with the כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's own wording already makes the exemption depend on the replacement being with the כהן, so רבי אלעזר's statement adds nothing

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי was only arguing on רבי מאיר's terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר is needed because we might have thought רבי יוסי himself exempts even without a replacement, for a different reason. On that reading, he only mentioned the replacement to win a point from רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי יוסי was speaking to רבי מאיר according to רבי מאיר's own view. 'In my view, it is exempt even if no replacement is with the כהן. If you obligate him in the gifts, he will come to shear the animal and work with it. But in your view, at least agree with me where the replacement is with the כהן, since the חכמים treated one who did not acquire as if he acquired.' And רבי מאיר said to him: 'No.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that רבי יוסי's words could have been read as only a debating move, so רבי אלעזר needed to tell us they are his real reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבי אלעזר, we might think רבי יוסי's true reason is to stop people from treating a possibly holy animal as ordinary, by shearing or working it. On that reading, the replacement line was only a smaller point he asked רבי מאיר to concede. רבי אלעזר teaches that the replacement really is רבי יוסי's own reason.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces the mistaken idea the statement comes to prevent
According to the words or view of the other side
Shearing and labor, which are forbidden with a בכור
At least concede to me
One who did not acquire, treated as if he acquired

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, רבי יוסי's real reason for the exemption is that the replacement is with the כהן. It was not just a debating point.
steps.confusionAlert: The whole speech of רבי יוסי here is only the 'might have thought' side. The גמרא is not saying this is how רבי יוסי actually reasons.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei was speaking to him according to Rabbi Meir's own view:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, אֲפִילּוּ אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: 'In my view, it is exempt even if no replacement is in the priest's hand,'
'because if you obligate him in the gifts,'
'he will come to shear it and work with it;'
phrases.notes: Giving the gifts makes it look like an ordinary animal, so he might forget it could be a holy בכור.

phrases.english: 'but in your view, at least concede to me'
'where the replacement is in the priest's hand,'
'that they treated one who did not acquire as one who acquired;'
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים. The כהן is treated as if he owns this animal too.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir said to him: 'No.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible misreading that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי exempts even without a replacement, to prevent shearing and labor. The replacement point was only a concession he asked of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר teaches that the replacement being with the כהן is רבי יוסי's real reason.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees a ספק מעשר is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that all agree an animal that may be מעשר is exempt from the priestly gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that a ספק מעשר animal is exempt from the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב פפא says that in the case of an animal that might be מעשר, both sides agree there is no obligation to give the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי was about a ספק בכור. רב פפא limits that argument. When the doubt is about מעשר, everyone holds the owner is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
An animal that may or may not be the tithe animal

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees regarding an animal that may be tithe
that it is exempt from the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ספק בכור to a related case, ספק מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספק מעשר animal is exempt from the priestly gifts according to everyone.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that רבי מאיר agrees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'everyone' must include. רבי מאיר only obligated a ספק בכור, because there the כהן has a claim either way. So it seems obvious he would exempt a ספק מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone agrees': who does that add? רבי מאיר? That is obvious! רבי מאיר only obligated there, by a ספק בכור, because the כהן comes at him from two sides. But by a ספק מעשר, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. It says his statement seems unnecessary, since רבי מאיר's reason obviously does not apply to a ספק מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a ספק בכור the כהן can claim either way: if it is a בכור, the animal is his; if not, the gifts are his. By a ספק מעשר the כהן has no such double claim. So why would anyone think רבי מאיר obligates it?

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious: a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
Only up to here: the opinion was stated only in this case
An animal that may or may not be a firstborn
From two sides: the כהן has a claim either way

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees': who is that?
Rabbi Meir? That is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָמְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir obligated there
only in the case of an animal that may be a firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּבָא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין,
phrases.english: since the priest comes at him from two sides,
phrases.notes: The כהן can say: if it's a בכור, give me the animal; if not, give me the gifts.

phrases.english: but by an animal that may be tithe, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַכֹּל מוֹדִים״ — מַאן? רַבִּי מֵאִיר? פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's statement in Step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב פפא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's reason, that the כהן comes from two sides, only fits a ספק בכור, so his agreement about ספק מעשר is obvious

steps.title: We might have thought רבי מאיר's reason is to keep the gifts remembered
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא is needed because we might have thought רבי מאיר obligates so that the laws of the gifts are not forgotten. That reason would apply to a ספק מעשר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי מאיר's reason is so that the law of the gifts not be forgotten, and then even a ספק מעשר would also be obligated. So רב פפא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows a different possible reason for רבי מאיר that would have made a ספק מעשר obligated, and רב פפא rules that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר's concern were only that people would forget about the gifts, it would not matter what kind of doubt there is. רב פפא teaches that רבי מאיר's reason is the כהן's two-sided claim. So by a ספק מעשר, everyone exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
So that the law of the gifts not be forgotten
He teaches us: the statement's new point

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר obligates a ספק בכור only because the כהן has a claim either way. Since that does not apply to a ספק מעשר, everyone agrees it is exempt.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the reason of Rabbi Meir
is so that the law of the gifts not be forgotten,
so even an animal that may be tithe would be obligated too?
He teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible misreading that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר obligates so that the gifts are not forgotten, which would include a ספק מעשר
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's reason is the כהן's two-sided claim, so a ספק מעשר is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to rule out that suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 5 that רבי מאיר might obligate a ספק מעשר. It points out that the משנה frames their argument around an animal whose replacement is with the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that? The end of the משנה teaches that רבי יוסי said: any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a כהן is exempt from the gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion that רבי מאיר obligates the gifts just so the laws are not forgotten. It points to the exact case the משנה chose for their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה presents their dispute only in the case where the כהן holds the replacement. That suggests רבי מאיר obligates because of the כהן's claim there, not because of a general worry about forgetting. If so, he would not obligate a ספק מעשר, and רב פפא's ruling again looks unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say this? (a formula that opens a challenge)
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Replacements: the animal given in exchange
The priestly gifts (foreleg, jaw and stomach)

phrases.english: And can you really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" is the idea from step 5, that רבי מאיר obligates the gifts so their laws are not forgotten.

phrases.english: But doesn't the latter clause teach,
that Rabbi Yosei would say:
any animal whose replacements are in the hand of a priest
is exempt from the gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 5 suggestion that רבי מאיר obligates in order that the gifts not be forgotten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה limits their argument to a case where the כהן holds the replacement. That implies רבי מאיר's reason is the כהן's claim, which does not exist for a ספק מעשר.

steps.title: Why רב פפא still needed to teach his ruling
steps.stepSummary: One could have read the משנה's case as chosen only to show how far רבי יוסי goes. On that reading, רבי מאיר might obligate even a ספק מעשר, so רב פפא teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי מאיר obligates even a ספק מעשר. Their argument about replacements would then be there only to show the strength of רבי יוסי, who exempts even where the כהן has a claim from two sides. So רב פפא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by offering another way to read the משנה. That reading would have misled us, so רב פפא's ruling is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case could have been picked to show רבי יוסי's bold view, not to limit רבי מאיר. Then רבי מאיר might obligate everywhere, even for a ספק מעשר. רב פפא's statement that 'all agree' rules out that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (how far a view reaches)
From two sides: the כהן has a claim whichever way the doubt falls
He teaches us (the new point being made)

steps.whatToRemember: All agree, even רבי מאיר, that a ספק מעשר is exempt from the priestly gifts.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲפִילּוּ סְפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר מְחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir obligates even an animal that may be tithe,
and the fact that they argue about replacements
is to show you the strength of Rabbi Yosei's view,
who exempts even where
the priest comes at him from two sides,
phrases.notes: The כהן has a claim either way: if it's a בכור, the whole animal is his; if not, he gets the gifts from it.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the purpose of the משנה's case (to show the strength of the other view)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר obligates even a ספק מעשר, and the replacement case only shows רבי יוסי's strength
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר too exempts a ספק מעשר, as רב פפא says

steps.title: The משנה: one twin died, רבי טרפון says divide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If one of the two males born together died, רבי טרפון rules that the כהן and the owner split the survivor.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two males were born together, and one of them was the בכור belonging to the כהן, but we do not know which. Now one has died, and רבי טרפון says the living one is shared.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide (split the value)
Firstborn male animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: If one of them died,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two males born together, where one is the כהן's בכור but we don't know which.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one of the twin males died, רבי טרפון says the כהן and owner divide the survivor

steps.title: Why divide? רבי טרפון's own logic should decide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they should divide. By רבי טרפון's own earlier view, the better animal goes to the כהן, so we can simply look at which one died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should they divide? Let us look: if the fat one died, it was the כהן's, and the one left is the owner's. If the thin one died, the owner's died, and the one left is the כהן's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי טרפון's ruling to divide. It argues that his own reasoning should tell us exactly who owns the survivor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי טרפון held that the כהן gets the better of the two animals. If so, there is no real doubt here: the fat one was the כהן's. Whichever one died, we know who owns the one that is left, so splitting makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let us look and see
Fat, the healthier animal
Thin, the weaker animal
The owner

phrases.english: Why should they divide?
Let us look:
if the fat one died
it is the priest's,
and this one that remains is the owner's;
and if the thin one died
the owner's died,
and this one that remains is the priest's!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי יַחְלוֹקוּ? נִיחְזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own earlier view gives the better animal to the כהן, which should settle who owns the survivor without any split.

steps.title: רבי טרפון changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that רבי טרפון retracted his earlier view that the כהן gets the better animal. So here the doubt is real, and they divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: רבי טרפון retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question by saying רבי טרפון took back his earlier position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי טרפון no longer says the כהן gets the better animal, we cannot know which twin was the בכור. That real doubt is why he rules that they divide.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted (changed his mind)

steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings of רבי טרפון still appear in the משנה. The ruling to divide is his later view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Rabbi Tarfon retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: חָזַר בּוֹ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the earlier view was given up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון still holds that the כהן gets the better animal
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון retracted, so there is a real doubt and they divide

steps.title: The משנה: רבי עקיבא's rule on the burden of proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה. Whoever wants to take something from someone else must bring proof, so the survivor stays with the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: one who wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the other opinion in the משנה, רבי עקיבא's. This sets the background for the parable in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animal is with the owner, the כהן is the one trying to take it. Without proof the כהן gets nothing, so the owner keeps the survivor.

keyTerms.meaning: One who wants to take from another must bring proof

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
one who takes from his fellow, the proof is on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the opposing view in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof; the survivor stays with the owner

steps.title: רבי חייא's shepherd parable for רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains רבי טרפון with a parable. Two people left sheep with a shepherd, and the shepherd leaves the remaining one between them. So the animal is in neither side's hands, and they split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: a parable for רבי טרפון's view. What is this like? Two people deposited animals with a shepherd. The shepherd puts the remaining one between them and walks away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives a parable to explain why רבי טרפון says to divide, even though רבי עקיבא's rule would leave the animal with the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule only works when one side already holds the item. In רבי חייא's picture, the shepherd holds it for neither side, so no one counts as the holder. That fits רבי טרפון: when the animal is in no one's hands, the doubt is split.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or comparison
To what is this comparable?
They deposited (left something in someone's care)
And he withdraws (steps away)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא may be looking at different cases: whether the animal is held by the owner or by no one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said:
A parable for Rabbi Tarfon's view:
to what is the matter comparable?
to two people who deposited with a shepherd,
phrases.notes: Each left a sheep, one died, and nobody knows whose it was.

phrases.english: where the shepherd places it between them and walks away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי טרפון's view against רבי עקיבא's rule from step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון's case is like a shepherd holding the item for neither side, so the two parties divide

steps.title: The parable for רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא gives a parable for רבי עקיבא: someone deposited a sheep with a homeowner, so the one who wants to take must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the parable for רבי עקיבא: What is this like? It is like someone who left a sheep with a homeowner. There, whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא now gives a second parable, this time to explain רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner has his own sheep, and someone left one more sheep with him. One sheep died, and nobody knows whose it was. The live sheep is in the homeowner's hands, so the other person must prove it is his. In the same way, the surviving animal stays with the owner unless the כהן brings proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a comparison
Deposited, left something in someone's care
A homeowner (here, someone who already has sheep of his own)
Whoever wants to take from another person must bring proof

phrases.english: And the parable for Rabbi Akiva's view:
To what is the matter comparable?
To one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner,
phrases.notes: The homeowner has sheep of his own too, and nobody knows whose sheep died.

phrases.english: where the one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching parable for רבי עקיבא, paired with רבי חייא's parable for רבי טרפון in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי עקיבא's view the case is like a sheep deposited with a homeowner: the animal stays where it is, and the claimant must prove his claim.

steps.title: So what are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: would רבי עקיבא really reject the shepherd parable, or רבי טרפון reject the homeowner parable? Both seem obviously true.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what are they arguing about? Does רבי עקיבא disagree about two people who left sheep with a shepherd, where the shepherd leaves the sheep and walks away? And does רבי טרפון disagree about one person who left a sheep with a homeowner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two parables. Both rules sound obviously correct, so how can the two תנאים be arguing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each parable states a basic, accepted rule about money. It is hard to believe רבי עקיבא would say the shepherd keeps the sheep, or that רבי טרפון would make a homeowner split what is in his own hands. So the parables alone cannot explain why they argue.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?
A shepherd (who watches sheep but does not own them)
Walks away, removes himself from the matter

steps.confusionAlert: These are not real questions asking for a yes or no. They are a challenge, meaning 'Surely neither one disagrees with these simple rules!'

phrases.english: But then, about what do they disagree?
Does Rabbi Akiva disagree
about two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd,
where the shepherd leaves it and walks away?
And does Rabbi Tarfon disagree
about one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two parables of steps 12-13, since both seem to be accepted by everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argue over the shepherd parable and the homeowner parable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both parables are basic rules that no one would reject, so they cannot be the source of the argument.

steps.title: Everyone agrees to both parables
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב פפא) says both parables are agreed by everyone: split in the shepherd case, and proof required in the homeowner case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רב פפא: Everyone agrees that when two people left sheep with a shepherd, the shepherd leaves the sheep between them and walks away. And when one person left a sheep with a homeowner, whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the challenge: there is no argument about either parable. This sets up his next point about where the argument really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules stand as agreed law. In the shepherd case, neither owner holds the sheep, so they split. In the homeowner case, he holds it, so the other side needs proof. The open question now is which of these cases the משנה matches.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (the statement is said in the name of someone else)
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rav Pappa:
Everyone agrees
about two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd
that the shepherd leaves it between them and walks away,
and about one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner
that the one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by agreeing that neither parable is in dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes both rules and moves the argument to a different question: which rule fits the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue over the parables themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parables are accepted by all; the argument is about which one our case resembles.

steps.title: The real case: owner's courtyard, כהן as shepherd
steps.stepSummary: The argument is only when the animals are in the owner's courtyard and the shepherd watching them is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree when the animals are in the owner's courtyard and the shepherd is a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now tells us exactly which case the משנה is talking about, and this sets up the two opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the animals sit in the owner's own courtyard, which points to the homeowner parable. But the person caring for them is a כהן, the one who would receive the בכור. So it is unclear which parable fits, and that is what they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagreed in (this case)
Courtyard (a person's property can acquire things for him)
A priest, who receives the firstborn animal

phrases.english: They only disagree
in the courtyard of the owner,
and the shepherd is a priest.
phrases.notes: This is the כהן the owner usually gives his firstborn animals to.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בַּחֲצַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וְרוֹעֶה כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer by naming the exact case where the תנאים disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument concerns animals in the owner's courtyard cared for by a כהן shepherd.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the owner gives the כהן a share in his courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון holds the owner gives the כהן a share of his courtyard, because he wants the מצוה done. So it is like the shepherd case, and they split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון holds: the owner gives the כהן ownership in his courtyard, because he is happy for a מצוה to be done with his property. So it is like two people who left sheep with a shepherd, where the shepherd leaves the sheep between them and walks away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי טרפון's reasoning in the courtyard case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard can acquire things for its owner. רבי טרפון says the owner wants the בכור to reach the כהן, so he gives the כהן a share in the courtyard. Now neither side fully holds the animal, just like the shepherd case, so they divide it.

keyTerms.meaning: He actually transfers ownership
He is pleased, it suits him
His property, his money

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon holds:
he transfers ownership to him in his courtyard,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the owner and 'him' is the כהן, who now has a share in the courtyard so it can acquire the בכור for him.

phrases.english: because he is pleased
that a מצוה be done with his property,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה,
phrases.english: and so it is like two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd,
where the shepherd leaves it between them and walks away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן סָבַר: אַקְנוֹיֵי קָא מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ בַּחֲצֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the case from step 16 to רבי טרפון, linking it to his shepherd parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the owner gives the כהן a share in the courtyard for the sake of the מצוה, neither side holds the animal, so they split it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the owner gives nothing when it might cost him
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds the owner gives the כהן nothing, since doing so might cost him. So it is like the homeowner case, and the כהן must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: since the owner could lose out, he gives the כהן nothing. So it is like one person who left a sheep with a homeowner, where whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי עקיבא's reasoning, which completes רבא's explanation of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is unclear which animal is the בכור, giving the כהן a share could cost the owner an animal. So he does not give one, and the courtyard stays fully his. The animal is in the owner's hands, so the כהן needs proof, just like the homeowner parable.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
A loss
Anything

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees to both parables. The only question is the owner's courtyard with a כהן shepherd: רבי טרפון says the owner shares his courtyard for the מצוה, so they split; רבי עקיבא says he would not give away something that might cost him, so the animal stays with the owner unless the כהן proves otherwise.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument is not about the rules of proof themselves. It is about what the owner probably intends: does wanting a מצוה beat worrying about a loss?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
since he would have a loss
phrases.notes: Since it is a doubt, giving the כהן a share could cost the owner an animal.

phrases.english: he does not transfer anything to him,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: and so it is like one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner,
where the one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's reasoning, the other half of the argument after רבי טרפון's in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument depends on whether the owner gives the כהן a share in his courtyard. רבי טרפון says yes, for the מצוה, so they split. רבי עקיבא says no, because of the possible loss, so the כהן must bring proof.

steps.title: Two first-time ewes: the simple cases
steps.stepSummary: If two ewes giving birth for the first time have two males, both go to the כהן. If they have a male and a female, the male goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man's two ewes had never given birth before, and they gave birth to two males, both go to the כהן. If they gave birth to a male and a female, the male goes to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the easy cases of two ewes giving birth for the first time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ewe's first lamb is a בכור. If there are two males, each ewe must have had one, so both are firstborn. If there is one male and one female, the male is surely its mother's first, so it is a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A ewe (female sheep)
Has already given birth for the first time
A firstborn male animal, which belongs to the כהן
A male

phrases.english: MISHNA:
His two ewes that had never given birth before
and they gave birth to two males
both of them go to the priest.
A male and a female:
the male goes to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי רְחֵילָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished explaining the dispute of רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two first-time ewes, every male that must be a firstborn goes to the כהן.

steps.title: Two males and a female: one to the owner, one to the priest
steps.stepSummary: With two males and a female, one male goes to the כהן and the owner keeps one. רבי טרפון says the כהן picks the better one. רבי עקיבא says they compare them and the כהן gets the leaner one. The second male must graze until it gets a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had two males and a female, one male is his and one goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the better one for himself. רבי עקיבא says: they compare the two, and the second one must graze until it gets a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a harder case where we know one male is a בכור but are unsure about the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ewe had a male. The other had a male and a female, but maybe the female came out first, so that male might not be a בכור. One male is surely a בכור and goes to the כהן. The other is only a maybe, so the owner keeps it but cannot use it until it gets a blemish. רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argue about which of the two the כהן gets.

keyTerms.meaning: Chooses
The better (nicer, fatter) one
They compare which one is fatter
It grazes (it is left in the pasture)
It gets a blemish (מום), so it can be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: מְשַׁמְּנִין does not mean they fatten the animals. It means they compare which one is fatter, and the כהן gets the leaner one.

phrases.english: Two males and a female:
one is his and one goes to the priest.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
the priest chooses for himself the better one.
Rabbi Akiva says:
they assess between them which is fatter,
and the second one grazes until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a harder case with three lambs, where one male is only a maybe-בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One male goes to the כהן. The other is a maybe-בכור and must graze until it gets a blemish. רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argue about which male the כהן receives.

steps.title: Must the owner give the priestly gifts from the second male?
steps.stepSummary: When the owner slaughters the second male after it gets a blemish, he must give the מתנות. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he must give the gifts from it. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a side rule about the second, maybe-בכור lamb once it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular animal that is slaughtered owes the כהן the foreleg, jaws and stomach. A real בכור does not, because the whole animal already belongs to the כהן. Since this lamb is only a maybe-בכור, the first opinion makes the owner give the מתנות, and רבי יוסי says he is exempt. His reason comes later in the משנה (step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts given to the כהן from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, jaws, stomach
Obligated
Exempts

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the gifts.
phrases.notes: The foreleg, jaws and stomach that go to a כהן from a slaughtered animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַיָּיב בַּמַּתָּנוֹת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the second male from step 20, now looking at the time it is slaughtered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: the owner gives the מתנות from the maybe-בכור. רבי יוסי: he is exempt.

steps.title: If one of the males died
steps.stepSummary: If one of the two males died, רבי טרפון says the owner and the כהן split. רבי עקיבא says whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they split it. רבי עקיבא says: the one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the case where one of the two males died before they were divided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is only one male, and we don't know whether it is the sure בכור or the maybe one. רבי טרפון says they split it. רבי עקיבא says the owner keeps it unless the כהן proves it is his. This is the same split-versus-proof argument the גמרא just explained in steps 14-18.

keyTerms.meaning: Died
They divide (split the value)
Whoever wants to take money from another must bring proof

phrases.english: If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide.
Rabbi Akiva says:
the one who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a twist to step 20: one of the two males is gone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: split the remaining lamb. רבי עקיבא: the owner keeps it unless the כהן brings proof.

steps.title: Cases where the priest gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: With two females and a male, or two males and two females, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had two females and a male, or two males and two females, the כהן gets nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the first-time-ewes section with cases where there is no sure בכור at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases each ewe may have had a female first. Then no male would be a בכור, so the כהן has no clear claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Females
There is not here
Anything at all

steps.whatToRemember: With two first-time ewes, the כהן gets only the males that must be firstborn. If a female could have come first from each ewe, he gets nothing.

phrases.english: Two females and a male,
or two males and two females:
the priest has nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the first set of cases by showing when the כהן's claim disappears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If each ewe could have had a female first, the כהן gets nothing.

steps.title: One ewe gave birth before, one did not: two males
steps.stepSummary: If one ewe had given birth before and the other had not, and they had two males, one goes to the כהן and the owner keeps one. The same רבי טרפון / רבי עקיבא argument applies, and the second male grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one ewe had given birth before and one had not, and they gave birth to two males, one is his and one goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the better one. רבי עקיבא says: they compare the two, and the second one grazes until it gets a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts its second set of cases: now only one of the ewes can have a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first-time ewe's male is a בכור. One of the two males is surely hers, but we don't know which one. So one goes to the כהן, and the other is a maybe-בכור that must graze until it gets a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: One ewe gave birth before, and one did not
And they gave birth (the text uses the singular form)
A doubt: we don't know which lamb is the בכור

phrases.english: One had given birth before
and one had not given birth before,
and they gave birth to two males:
one is his and one goes to the priest.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
the priest chooses the better one.
Rabbi Akiva says:
they assess between them which is fatter,
and the second one grazes until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה וְאַחַת לֹא בִּיכְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rules of step 20 for a new setup, where only one ewe can have a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One male goes to the כהן, the other is a maybe-בכור and grazes. The argument over which male the כהן gets is the same as before.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains why the gifts are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The owner must give the מתנות from the second male. רבי יוסי exempts him, because anything whose replacement is already with the כהן is exempt. רבי מאיר obligates him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he must give the gifts. רבי יוסי exempts him, because רבי יוסי says: any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a כהן is exempt from the gifts. And רבי מאיר obligates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the argument about the מתנות, and this time it gives רבי יוסי's reason and names רבי מאיר as the one who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's idea: the כהן already received one of the two males to cover the בכור. So the owner can say about this one, 'If it is the בכור, you already have its replacement.' That is why he is exempt from the מתנות. רבי מאיר still obligates him.

keyTerms.meaning: Its replacement (what stands in place of it)
In the hand of a כהן
The תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי here
Obligates

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the short line 'רבי יוסי פוטר' from step 21 as well. Both cases follow the same reason.

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the gifts.
Rabbi Yosei exempts him,
as Rabbi Yosei says:
any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a priest
phrases.notes: The כהן already got one of the pair, which stands in for this one.

phrases.english: is exempt from the gifts.
And Rabbi Meir obligates him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the gifts argument from step 21 for the new case and adds רבי יוסי's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: an animal whose replacement is already with the כהן is exempt from מתנות. רבי מאיר: he must give them.

steps.title: One male died: the same argument again
steps.stepSummary: If one of the two males died, רבי טרפון says they split, and רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they split it. רבי עקיבא says: the one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the split-versus-proof argument to the new case of one experienced ewe and one first-time ewe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again only one male is left, and we don't know whether it is the בכור. רבי טרפון splits it. רבי עקיבא leaves it with the owner unless the כהן brings proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Of them
His fellow (the other side)
A money doubt: we don't know who really owns it

phrases.english: If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide.
Rabbi Akiva says:
the one who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same dispute as step 22, now in the case of one experienced ewe and one first-time ewe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: split. רבי עקיבא: the owner keeps it unless the כהן brings proof.

steps.title: A male and a female: the priest gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If one ewe had given birth before and they had a male and a female, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had a male and a female, the כהן gets nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a case where the כהן has no claim at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the ewe that already gave birth had the male, and the first-time ewe had the female. In that case no male is a בכור, so the כהן cannot take anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A male and a female
The first to open the womb: the animal that counts as the firstborn
A doubtful firstborn

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן gets a lamb only when at least one male must be a בכור. When there is a doubt about which male it is, one male goes to the כהן and the other grazes until it gets a blemish. If no male has to be a בכור, the כהן gets nothing.

phrases.english: A male and a female:
the priest has nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the second set of cases with the case where the כהן's claim disappears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With one experienced ewe, a male and a female give the כהן nothing, since the male may belong to the experienced ewe.

steps.title: Why the first case alone was not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all the cases were needed. From the first case alone (one ewe, two males), we might think רבי עקיבא would agree with רבי טרפון in the two-ewe case.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: All the cases were necessary. If the משנה had taught only the first case, we would say רבי עקיבא holds his view there, because both babies came from one mother. But with two ewes that had never given birth, where one mother had two babies and the other had one, we might say he agrees with רבי טרפון, because the baby whose mother had only one is stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining why the משנה repeated the same argument in more than one case. It starts with why the first case did not make the second case unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, both males came from one mother, so there is no reason to think the better one came out first, and רבי עקיבא says the כהן gets the leaner one. In the two-ewe case, one animal was born alone, and a baby born alone is usually stronger. So we might think רבי עקיבא would admit the כהן gets the better one there. The משנה had to teach that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (each case had to be taught)
It taught us
The first case
I might have said (a mistaken idea we could have had)
He agrees with him
Is stronger / of better quality

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is necessary,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is explaining why the משנה needed to list all three cases of the same argument.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us only the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the one ewe that gave birth to two males, from the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: in that case רבי עקיבא said his view,
since the two came from one mother.
But with his ewes that had not given birth before,
where two came from one mother and one came from the other,
I might say he agrees with רבי טרפון,
since the one born to the mother that bore only one is stronger.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's cases into the גמרא, explaining why the repeated argument appears in each case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two-ewe case had to be taught, because from the one-ewe case alone we might think רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון when one baby was born alone and is likely stronger.

steps.title: Why the second case alone was not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues: from the two-ewe case alone we might think רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון when one ewe had given birth before and the two gave birth to two males. The reason comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only this second case, we would say רבי עקיבא holds his view there, because neither ewe had given birth before. But if one had given birth before and one had not, and they gave birth to two males, I might say he agrees with רבי טרפון...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next link in the chain: why the second case does not make the third case unnecessary. This sets up a reason that the גמרא gives in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, both ewes had never given birth, so both are on equal footing. The third case is different: one ewe had already given birth, so only the other ewe's male is a real בכור. The גמרא says that here we might think רבי עקיבא would agree with רבי טרפון, and it explains why right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: Had already given birth before (her firstborn is behind her)
Both of them
Males

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this second case,
in this case רבי עקיבא said his view,
since both had not given birth before,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה
phrases.english: but where one had given birth before and one had not,
and they gave birth to two males,
I might say he agrees with רבי טרפון,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא chain: after showing why the second case was needed, it begins to show why the third case was needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the case where both ewes had never given birth, we might think רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון when one ewe had given birth before and they bore two males. The reason follows in the next lines.
